text:
A: Alright? Darren. Can you hear me okay?
B: Erm, yes. Hi. I'm Kezia.
A: Hello, Kezia. Where's that to, then?
B: Catford. South East London.
A: Lovely. I'm Bridgwater, Somerset. Long way from you, mind. Here, I've got to say, I saw that sign on your wall in your photo. "Be still and know that I am God." I liked that.
B: Oh. Thank you. My mum bought it me when I moved into the flat.
A: That's nice, that. I'm not a big churchgoer, Christmas and Easter really, but I still say a little prayer when things go wrong. Do you go regular?
B: Most Sundays, yeah. With my mum. And I sing in the choir. Alto.
A: Alto! Go on then, that's the middle one, is it?
B: Erm, sort of the lower one for women. You don't get the tune, you get the bit underneath. I practise the parts at home so I don't mess it up.
A: Ha, I'd be no good, I only know the tune to anything. Madness, UB40, that's my level. What do you do for work?
B: I'm a teaching assistant. SEN, at a primary in Lewisham. Two little ones with autism, in Year 3.
A: Oh, that's a proper job, that is. Patience of a saint, I bet.
B: Erm, I don't know. You just get to know them. What do you do?
A: Flooring and tiles in a big DIY place in Taunton. I'm the bloke you ask when you don't know what grout is. Which is most people, to be fair. I had a fella last week wanted to tile his whole bathroom in an afternoon. I told Gemma that one earlier and she just looked at me.
B: I spoke to Gemma as well. She was nice. Quite, sort of, direct.
A: She is, yeah, I liked her. Proper no-nonsense. So what's a good day for you, then, with the kids?
B: Erm. When nothing changes, honestly. If the routine holds, they're happy, I'm happy. There's one boy who used his now-and-next board on his own last week. That was a good day.
A: Now-and-next board, what's that when it's at home?
B: It's pictures. What we're doing now, and what's next. So he knows what's coming and he's not worried about it.
A: Do you know what, I could do with one of them. Now: work. Next: skittles. Then I'd be fine all week.
B: Ha. Yeah. I've got a planner that's sort of the same thing, with stickers. Is that okay, sorry, is that a weird thing to say?
A: No, not at all! My daughter Kayleigh's the same, she's twenty, works in a nail salon, everything's colour-coded. Her nails, her diary, the lot. Me, I can't remember to log a box on the handheld.
B: I do my own braids. That takes about a whole weekend.
A: A whole weekend! Kayleigh'd be well impressed, she's always on about braids. Do you go away much, holidays and that?
B: Not really. Jamaica with family. My mum's from there. And Tenerife once. Mostly I go to Birmingham on the coach to see my auntie.
A: Tenerife! We did Tenerife twice. Lovely weather, hated the airport. Cornwall caravan's more my speed. Do you get nervous flying?
B: Yeah, a bit. Airports, mainly. All the queues and the announcements.
A: Oh, don't. Bristol Airport, I said to Donna, I'm not doing that again, and then she booked it again—
